answers.why: The man of God comes from Judah, identifying the territory of the kingdom.
Judah is the territory from which the man of God came to Bethel.
The prophet asks whether this is the man of God who came from Judah's territory.
The addressed man of God is identified as having come from Judah's territory.
The LORD is called the God of the nation over which he appointed Jeroboam.
Israel is explicitly God's people over whom Jeroboam was made ruler.
Those of Jeroboam's house are to be cut off within the kingdom of Israel.
All Israel collectively will mourn and bury Jeroboam's child.
The LORD God of Israel is the nation's God toward whom the child showed goodness.
The LORD will raise up a king over Israel to destroy Jeroboam's dynasty.
Israel is the nation the LORD will strike because its people made idolatrous groves.
Israel will be uprooted from its ancestral land and its people scattered beyond the river.
The LORD will give up the nation because of Jeroboam's sins.
Jeroboam caused the people of Israel to sin.
All Israel collectively mourned Jeroboam's child after his burial.
Rehoboam reigned in Judah, the kingdom centered on Jerusalem.
Judah's collective wrongdoing is described with plural references to their sins and fathers.
